units.name: command-tree
units.role: Define what a command is, assemble commands into a tree, and run the one the user asked for.
units.description: This is the heart of Cobra. It defines what a 'command' is (its name, description, help text, flags, and the function that runs when it is invoked), lets a program assemble commands into a tree of commands and subcommands, and figures out which command the user actually typed on the command line, including tolerating abbreviations and offering 'did you mean' suggestions on typos. Once it knows the target command, it parses that command's flags, runs its setup/run/cleanup steps in the right order, and prints help text, usage instructions, version information, and error messages. On Windows it also detects whether the program was double-clicked from Explorer (rather than run from a terminal) and shows a short explanatory message instead of flashing and closing. Almost everything else in Cobra is a plug-in that this core tree calls into or is called by.

units.name: args-validators
units.role: Provide ready-made rules for how many positional arguments a command accepts.
units.description: This is a small toolbox of ready-made rules for checking the plain words typed after a command name (as opposed to flags like --verbose). A command author picks one of these rules - for example, 'exactly two arguments', 'at least one', 'none at all', or 'a number in this range' - or combines several together, and assigns it to a command. Cobra then automatically runs that rule before the command's action executes and produces a friendly error message if the user typed the wrong number or kind of arguments. It contains no networking, file, or system access; it is pure decision-making about argument counts and values.

units.name: flag-groups
units.role: Enforce rules about which flags must, may, or must not be used together.
units.description: This code implements rules for grouping command-line flags together: a command can declare that certain flags must all be used together, that at least one flag from a set must be given, or that flags in a set are mutually exclusive so only one of them may be used at a time. It checks these rules whenever a command actually runs and produces a clear error if the user violates them, and it feeds the same rules into the shell auto-completion system so suggestions respect the grouping.

units.name: completion-engine
units.role: Decide, at Tab-press time, which subcommands, flags, and values are valid next.
units.description: This is the brain of Cobra's shell tab-completion feature. It decides, at the moment a user presses Tab in their terminal, what suggestions are valid: which subcommands, which flags, which flag values, or which custom-defined choices apply given what has been typed so far. It works by silently walking the command tree the same way normal execution would, but instead of running the command it collects the list of legal next words plus a 'directive' telling the shell how to treat them (for example, don't add a trailing space, or filter by file extension). It exposes this through a hidden completion command that shell-specific scripts invoke, and lets application authors register their own completion logic for individual flags or arguments. It does not generate the shell scripts themselves - that rendering is a separate concern - it only supplies the decision logic and shared vocabulary that those renderers embed into their output.

units.name: doc-generators
units.role: Turn a command tree into man pages, Markdown, ReStructuredText, or YAML documentation files.
units.description: This part of the code turns a Cobra command-line application into human- and machine-readable documentation files. Given the tree of commands and subcommands that make up a CLI tool, it can automatically write out Unix man pages, Markdown pages, ReStructuredText pages, or YAML reference files describing every command, its flags, its usage examples, and links between parent and child commands. Its job is to talk to the filesystem and to external documentation toolchains, rather than to encode what the CLI tool itself does.

units.name: cobra-runtime-utils
units.role: Package-wide plumbing: template-function registry, lifecycle hooks, and output/string helpers.
units.description: This is a small toolbox of generic helpers and global settings that the rest of Cobra leans on, but which are not about what any specific command does. It provides a registry where extra template functions can be plugged in for rendering help and usage text, global 'run this before/after every command' hooks, output helpers that print an error and stop the program or write text and check for failure, and a couple of package-wide on/off switches (such as case-insensitive command names) plus the Windows 'mousetrap' warning text and timing.

violations_observed.note: legacyArgs is command.go's default fallback validator, but it is defined in args.go and calls the unexported Command.findSuggestions method directly instead of through a documented API. Conversely, command.go's Find/execute call the unexported legacyArgs itself. Both directions bypass any exported contract; only Go's single-package visibility makes this compile.

flag_groups.go calls the unexported Command.mergePersistentFlags to make sure inherited flags are visible before validating groups, reaching past command-tree's public Flags()/PersistentFlags() accessors.

completions.go reads command.go's unexported struct fields (ctx, parent, commands, helpCommand, completionCommandGroupID) and calls unexported package-level helpers isFlagArg, FlagSetByCobraAnnotation and constants helpFlagName/helpCommandName, rather than going through Command's public methods.
command.go calls completions.go's unexported method Command.initCompleteCmd to wire up the hidden __complete command; only InitDefaultCompletionCmd is an intentional public entrypoint.
The bash completion generators read command.go's unexported Command.helpCommand field directly instead of via a public accessor.
completions.go calls bash_completions.go's unexported nonCompletableFlag helper.
active_help.go builds its environment-variable name using completions.go's unexported configEnvVar and configEnvVarGlobalPrefix instead of active-help defining its own naming helper.

Every shell script generator embeds active_help.go's unexported activeHelpMarker constant and calls its unexported activeHelpEnvVar function to emit the active-help protocol into generated scripts, rather than active-help exposing these as a public constant/function.
completions.go calls flag_groups.go's unexported Command.enforceFlagGroupsForCompletion method.

command.go calls cobra.go's unexported helpers tmpl, ld, rpad and trimRightSpace, and reads/appends to its unexported package-level slices initializers/finalizers, rather than through an exported API.
cobra.go's tmpl() constructs a value of command.go's unexported tmplFunc struct type, making the coupling between these two units bidirectional rather than layered.
args.go calls cobra.go's unexported stringInSlice helper instead of a public string-membership utility.
